mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the company's proposed Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social) for name reservation and registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) after pre-approval of the corporate name

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of each director's, officer's, and shareholder's passport or government-issued ID
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the individual's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Certificate of Incumbency or Corporate Existence from the jurisdiction of any foreign legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry or Corporate Registrar in the foreign shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed financial institution where the beneficial owner maintains the account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners against OFAC SDN list, United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union restrictive measures, and Panama's internal consolidated sanctions list maintained by the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF). Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP), including identification of source of wealth, source of funds, and family and close associate connections. A qualified AML compliance officer must sign a risk assessment and maintain ongoing transaction monitoring under Law 23 of 2015 and UAF regulatory guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sistema de Trámites en Línea (online corporate name reservation portal at www.registro-publico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory corporate names must be submitted in Spanish. Non-Spanish names and foreign script transliterations must be rendered in Spanish phonetic or Latin-character form. The registry applies strict orthographic rules, disallows misleading abbreviations that create confusion with existing entities, and requires the use of legal suffixes recognized under Panamanian corporate law, such as 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) with the General Directorate of the Panama Public Registry within 5 business days of the rejection notice. The appeal must identify the proposed name, the statutory basis for rejection, and a legal argument demonstrating conformity with registry naming regulations. If the administrative appeal is denied, a further contentious-administrative complaint (demanda contencioso-administrativa) may be filed before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice within 2 months of the final administrative decision. During the appeal, the applicant may simultaneously reserve an alternative eligible name with the registry portal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The use of a virtual office is generally permissible for a Panama S.A. provided that the company appoints a licensed resident agent (agente residente) whose registered address in Panama is used as the statutory statutory address. For the proposed HealthTech EMR SaaS activity, no physical land-based clinic is required; the virtual office will not impede licensing as long as the resident agent maintains a physical reception for official notifications. However, if the company intends to contract with Panamanian public healthcare institutions or process health data that falls under the 'Ministerio de Salud' regulatory purview, a physical local compliance contact or data processor address may be required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate (estimated 12% annual probability for a non-financial professional B2B SaaS entity engaged in medical data processing, but increasing to 25% if the company registers as a data processor under Panamanian health-data regulations). The Panama Public Registry and the Gaceta Oficial publication process do not conduct on-site inspections; the Directorate General of Revenue and the Ministry of Health may perform documentary or surprise audits of a medical-data company, especially to verify data privacy safeguards and commercial substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (General Corporation Law of Panama), as amended — Arts. 2 (incorporation by public deed), 7/13 (registered office and resident agent), 25 (capital subscription and payment), 57-72 (board of directors and officers); read together with Registro Público regulations and Ley No. 129 de 2020 on beneficial-owner transparency. Ley No. 58 de 2015 (Simplified Stock Corporation 'SAS') remains available as a streamlined alternative.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil y de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile and Legal Persons Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima (Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Pacto Social (Articles of Incorporation) and Estatutos (Bylaws), recorded in the Mercantile Register of the Public Registry of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital exists; no capital escrow or deposit account is required. The charter commonly declares USD 10,000 nominal capital divided into 100 common shares of USD 100 par value each, which may be subscribed at incorporation and paid in later. Bearer shares are permitted but trigger beneficial-ownership reporting under Ley No. 129 de 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION No. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY], S.A. WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated by public deed under Republic of Panama Law 32 of 1927 and inscribed in the Public Registry; and WHEREAS, the subscribers appointed the undersigned as first Directors; NOW, THEREFORE, UNANIMOUSLY RESOLVED: (1) Subscription of the Company's authorized shares by the named incorporators is ratified and share issuance approved; (2) The registered office is fixed at [Panama address], and [Law Firm] is appointed Resident Agent; (3) [NAME] is elected President, [NAME] Secretary, and [NAME] Treasurer, each to hold office until successor election; (4) The Officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and take every act to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Ventanilla de Personas Jurídicas / E-Registry online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-clearance application (certificado de no inscripción) stating the proposed corporate name and the sectoral object, i.e., ISIC 6201 computer programming and EMR cloud software. The Registry verifies that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing commercial folio; after clearance, the name is secured for use in the public deed.
required_dossiers: Completed name-clearance application form
Passport or cédula copies of the incorporating subscribers
Proposed corporate name plus up to two alternative names
Corporate purpose summary (software development, EMR services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry objects on similarity grounds, file a reconsideration brief distinguishing the names, or adopt one of the pre-selected alternative names and re-file; the clearance certificate may be re-requested at a minimal fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría del Circuito de Panamá (Notary Public of the Judicial Circuit)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The subscribers appear before the Panamanian notary, personally or by power of attorney, and execute the Escritura Pública de Constitución containing the corporate name, object clause (EMR clinical workflow software and related services), authorized share capital, directors, resident agent, and registered office. The notary protocolizes the deed and issues certified copies for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Name-clearance certificate issued by the Public Registry
Passports or cédulas of all subscribing shareholders
Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if any subscriber is absent
Draft Pacto Social and Estatutos
Resident agent's written acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary returns the draft for formal defects, correct the deficient clauses and execute a rectification addendum; the re-executed deed is then forwarded directly to the Public Registry without resetting the original corporate date if filed promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Inscription in the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified copy of the Escritura Pública together with the registration petition and proof of fee payment. The Registry verifies the corporate name, object, capital, appointed directors, resident agent, and registered office. Upon inscription, the Registry assigns a legal-entity folio (Ficha) and the corporation acquires full legal personality; a certificado de inscripción is issued for subsequent tax and banking use.
required_dossiers: First certified copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución
Registration petition (petición de inscripción) signed by a licensed Panamanian attorney
Receipt of payment of registry inscription fees and stamp duties
Resident-agent clause and acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice (nota de defecto), the attorney must cure the observations within 30 days by filing supplementary documents or a corrective notarial addendum; if the deadline lapses, a new priority filing is required with the same deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formalization of Registered Office and Resident Agent Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Resident Agent (licensed Panamanian attorney) under supervision of the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The resident agent executes its formal acceptance in the deed and maintains the registered-office file at the stated Panama address. The agent receives government and court correspondence, keeps the corporate records, and ensures compliance with the annual registry fees, beneficial-owner declaration, and tax filings under Ley No. 129 de 2020.
required_dossiers: Inscription certificate (Ficha) from the Public Registry
Signed resident-agency agreement
Beneficial-owner identification and KYC forms for the AML file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the resident agent resigns or is removed, the board adopts a resolution appointing a substitute licensed agent, and the change is recorded in the Public Registry with the new agent's acceptance and applicable filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Municipal Operating Permit Registration (RUC and Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá (Ventanilla Única del Contribuyente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the DGI pre-registration to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) for the corporation, designating the activity as CIIU 6201 — Programación Informática (software publishing and EMR cloud services). After the RUC is issued, apply for the municipal Aviso de Operación at the Municipality of Panama, presenting the lease contract or registered-office confirmation. The Aviso constitutes the operational commercial license and fixes the municipal tax obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificado de inscripción from the Public Registry
Certified copy of the Escritura Pública
Corporate power of attorney for the legal representative
Lease contract or registered-office domiciliation certificate
Passport or cédula copies of directors and officers
RUC application form (DGI) and municipal forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the application due to missing supporting documents, submit the corrected corporate dossier through the 'Ventanilla Única'; if the municipality rejects the Aviso for an address mismatch, update the municipal constancia and re-file the application electronically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security, Labor Registry, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS); Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); licensed Panamanian bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the corporation as an employer with the CSS for payroll contributions and register the labor records with MITRADEL if staff will be engaged. Hold the first formal board meeting to approve share issuance, adopt the corporate books (share ledger, minutes book), and authorize the opening of a corporate bank account. The bank will conduct KYC and may require the beneficial-owner declaration and corporate folio certificate.
required_dossiers: RUC and Certificado de Aviso de Operación
Corporate folio certificate (Ficha) and list of directors
Beneficial-owner declaration under Ley No. 129 de 2020
Share subscription list and board minutes approving share issuance
CSS employer pre-registration forms and proposed payroll data
Bank KYC forms, business plan, and reference letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CSS or MITRADEL objections are cured by correcting payroll and job classifications; a bank's KYC refusal is cured by completing the beneficial-owner filing with the DGI or Public Registry and resubmitting the dossier either to the same bank or to an alternative licensed institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — technology services sector; Municipalidad de Panamá for the commercial Aviso de Operación; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) if the EMR is clinically classified as health software
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Notice of Operation) — municipal commercial operating permit; optional MINSA certification for clinical/health-information software

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Categoría I (low impact) / registration only — cloud-based EMR SaaS generates no physical manufacturing discharges and is exempt from a full EIA Study; a simple environmental registration or certification may be required for the office premises
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Ley No. 41 de 1998 (General Environment Law) and Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009: no industrial wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous air emissions are generated; domestic office wastewater is discharged to the municipal sewerage system; electronic waste and end-of-life IT equipment must be handled through MiAMBIENTE-licensed recyclers under the national WEEE and solid-waste rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá — fire-safety inspection certificate and compliance with the National Fire Prevention Code for the registered office; MINSA occupational-health clearance for office workplaces; MITRADEL workplace-safety and evacuation plan filings; structural load and electrical safety compliance certificates from the Municipality where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa (also via Sede Electrónica: https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first appoint a resident legal representative and register with the Public Registry (Registro Público) to obtain corporate existence. Then, apply for a taxpayer identification number (RUC – Registro Único de Contribuyente) via the DGI's online portal or in person. The application requires the corporate charter, proof of registered agent, and identification of directors. The RUC is issued immediately upon completion of the online form and validation of documents. For VAT purposes, the same RUC serves as the VAT ID. Non-resident entities without a permanent establishment may need to register only for specific transactions, but for a local S.A. with business activity, full registration is mandatory.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not offer check-the-box elections. However, entities may elect to be taxed as a Panama International Company (Sociedad Anónima) under the territorial regime, which taxes only Panama-source income. There is no hybrid mismatch election; Panama's tax law does not recognize hybrid entities. For transfer pricing, entities may elect to apply the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines, but this is not a classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – VAT equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold; any person or entity engaged in taxable activities (sale of goods or services) in Panama must register for ITBMS. However, small taxpayers with annual gross income below USD 36,000 may opt for the simplified regime (Régimen Simplificado) with a reduced rate of 2% on sales, but this is optional. For standard VAT registration, there is no threshold; registration is mandatory from the first taxable operation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all taxpayers. The DGI's 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' (SFE) requires real-time transmission of invoices to the DGI via API or web portal. Taxpayers must obtain digital authorization (Aviso de Facturación) and use digital stamps (Código QR) on each invoice. The system requires integration with the DGI's web services (API) for validation and clearance. Since 2023, all taxpayers must issue electronic invoices; non-compliance results in fines and suspension of operations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated for ITBMS. For services, the service must be rendered to a non-resident client, and the benefit of the service must be deemed to occur outside Panama. For software/SaaS, the service must be provided to a foreign entity and not be used or consumed in Panama. The taxpayer must maintain evidence of the export, including the contract, proof of payment from abroad, and a declaration that the service is for foreign use. The DGI may require a certificate of non-residence of the client.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) – for goods, but for services, a 'Declaración de Servicios Exportados' is required
Commercial Invoice or Contract detailing the service
Proof of payment from abroad (e.g., SWIFT, bank transfer receipt)
Certificate of Non-Residence of the client (if applicable)
RUC registration and ITBMS registration certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims. If the export is found to be fraudulent or not substantiated, the taxpayer is liable for the unpaid ITBMS (7%) plus interest (currently 1% per month) and fines up to 200% of the tax due. Additionally, criminal penalties may apply for tax fraud, including imprisonment. The DGI has a 5-year statute of limitations for assessments, but in cases of fraud, the period extends to 10 years. Retroactive clawbacks are common when documentation is incomplete.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama does not operate a central bank. Monetary and banking supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP), while the official currency issuer is the National Bank of Panama (Banco Nacional de Panama) acting as the government's fiscal agent. For foreign exchange, there is no separate FX administration; the SBP regulates banking and forex market participants, and the Superintendencia de Sujetos no Bancarios supervises non-bank financial entities, including foreign exchange exchange houses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction under which the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a nominal unit on par with the US Dollar (USD) and USD coin and paper currency circulate freely as legal tender. There are no capital controls, no exchange controls, and no differentiated current versus capital account restrictiveness. Profit repatriation, dividend distributions, and return of capital can be freely executed in USD through commercial banks without prior central bank authorization. The only material hurdle is corporate income tax compliance on Panama-source income, including a 10% dividend withholding tax on dividends declared from Panama-source profits and a 2% management fee tax on payments to non-resident directors, if applicable. The absence of an FX regime makes currency convertibility effectively 100% unrestricted for operational and treasury purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no statutory conversion, surrender, or repatriation requirements on export proceeds. Exporters, including software and cloud service providers, may receive invoices in USD or any other freely convertible currency, maintain offshore collections, and use export receipts for any lawful purpose. The only applicable duty is the obligation to keep proper books and records for tax purposes under the territorial income tax regime and to bank through SBP-licensed institutions when such funds are routed through Panamanian bank accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational USD Current Account
Operational Account with dedicated International Transfer Routing and Escrow KYC Wallet
Commingled Operational and Treasury Clearing Account
Capital Injection Escrow Account and Day-to-Day Treasury Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Caja de Ahorros (Panama State Savings Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium. Panama does not recognize the EU EMI (Electronic Money Institution) passport, and offshore digital EMI entities without an SBP banking or fintech license cannot establish a local settlement account. In practice, a licensed Panamanian digital bank or a fully authorized fintech payment processor (e.g., STRIKE-backed USD settlement rails, or a SBP-licensed 'red multibanco' participant) may be used as a local clearing agent, but this requires an SBP-filed outsourcing arrangement and a compliant anti-money laundering KYC file. The most practical route for a foreign-owned EMR SaaS is to maintain a Tier 1 commercial bank account and deploy Stripe Billing as a front-end payment rail while clearing through the licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For newly incorporated Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) clients with non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), most Panamanian Tier 1 banks require at least one authorized signer or entity director to appear physically at a Panamanian branch for the KYC interview and risk appetite screening. Remote opening is possible if the bank accepts digital identity verification, apostilled corporate documents, and notarized power of attorney executed at a Panama consulate; however, the final decision rests with the bank's compliance committee. It is strongly advisable to appoint a Panama-resident legal or corporate agent with bank introduction capacity to avoid prolonged onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and UBOs who are nationals of or tax resident in high-risk FATF-monitored jurisdictions or jurisdictions with non-transparent beneficial ownership laws.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled certificate of incorporation and bylaws (notarized to the SBP standard), certified copy of the UBO register or director register, current passport copies for each director and UBO, independent proof of residential address issued within the last 3 months, reference letters from a qualifying foreign bank or regulated law firm, and a written declaration of economic substance in Panama detailing the EMR SaaS activity and the role of the Panamanian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of bearer-share structures or unregistered bearer-share certificates issued before the Panama bearer-share mandatory immobilization regime.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalization certificate from the SBP or the Public Registry showing the entity is in full compliance with Law 47 of 2013 and subsequent reforms, a sworn affidavit confirming no bearer shares are outstanding, and a resolution of the board of directors directing the cancellation or immobilization of any legacy bearer share certificates with the physical instruments delivered to the corporate agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound capital injection from a corporate group with insufficient public commercial background.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A board resolution of the parent entity authorizing the capital contribution, audited financial statements or an equivalent financial solvency letter, corporate registration certificate of the parent, commercial invoice or signed SaaS master services agreement proving the economic purpose, source-of-funds evidence via bank statements of the remitting entity for at least 3 months, and a Panama corporate tax filing projection showing the injected capital is classified as contributed capital rather than revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign director signature sample mismatch or lack of physical signature verification during onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized signature cards for every authorized signatory, apostilled corporate minutes granting signature authority, a medallion-guaranteed signature guarantee from a US-registered bank if the signor is in the United States, and an unexpired government-issued passport or national identity card with a matching notarized copy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial transaction profile with cross-border data hosting and recurring payments that triggers excessive intermediary screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A written privacy and data processing policy showing compliance with Panama's Law 81 of 2019 on personal data (or proof that health data is processed in a HIPAA-compliant cloud environment), documentation of the US counterparty or Panama-rooted clinical customer relationship, and a detailed sanctions screening report confirming that neither the ultimate holding company nor any counterparty appears on OFAC, EU, UN, or national CFT lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing follows a normal USD wire transfer via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign parent or investor account to the Panamanian entity's local account. Since Panama uses US dollar clearing, all inbound incoming wires settle through Fedwire, CHIPS, or correspondent banking networks, and the receiving Panamanian bank will typically request a Funds Receipt Form. The recommended payment purpose description is 'Equity capital contribution to Panamanian subsidiary — No services rendered' or 'Paid-in capital deposit under Law 32 of 1927, S.A. incorporation'. Supporting verification includes the board resolution approving the capital increase, a sworn statement before the SBP-compliant compliance officer, and identification of the ultimate source of funds. If the remittance exceeds existing paid-in capital limits, the entity must update the registry at the Public Registry (Registro Público) within the statutory corporate filing window and ensure the increase is reflected in the tax registration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for licensing fees, software vendor payments, and cloud infrastructure settlements are executed via SWIFT MT103 credit transfers for direct commercial payments and via MT202 for interbank reimbursements when routing through a correspondent bank. For high-value medical clinic software licensing to Panamanian clinics, the preferred instrument is a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) where the Panamanian buyer initiates a documentary LC through the issuing bank, with the beneficiary collecting against presentation of an electronic software license certificate or commercial invoice. Cross-border cash concentration may be achieved by using a single USD sweeping account in Panama with a US correspondent bank, thereby reducing the clearing time to same-day via Fedwire and enabling straight-through-processing to Stripe Billing vaults. No local FX conversion is required because both the remitting parent and the Panamanian S.A. operate in USD.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/PAB spot and forward contracts (where the PAB is conceptually converted at 1.00, these are primarily notional).
Cross-currency swaps (USD against EUR, CHF, or LATAM currencies) with SBP-licensed counterparties.
FX forwards against non-convertible regional currencies (e.g., COP, MXN) for head-office settlements.
FX options (plain vanilla call/put) available from large international banks through the Panamanian branch.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on currencies with offshore restrictions, permitted when arranged through a global bank and settled in USD outside Panama; although PAB is fixed, NDF instruments are not prohibited by Panamanian law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Panama Annual Corporate Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades - IAS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; payment processed through the Panama Tax Administration electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January to 15 March of each calendar year; no administrative extension available for this franchise tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 15 March triggers a 10% surcharge (US$30). Non-payment through 31 July exposes the S.A. to additional DGI collection enforcement and administrative strike-off/dissolution proceedings before the Public Registry of Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta - Form 22)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March following the calendar fiscal year-end; extended only by express DGI resolution for specified categories
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing with understated Panama-source income subjects the S.A. to fines equivalent to 5% to 15% of tax due, plus variable monthly interest and potential criminal referral for tax fraud.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements (Dictamen del Contador Público Autorizado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); minutes of the shareholders' meeting retained in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, the independent auditor's report and audited financial statements must accompany the income tax return by 15 March when the audit threshold is met.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a Panamanian CPA and submit audited statements when required can result in DGI fines and nullification of claimed deductions or tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Corporate Records Confirmation (continuous registered office maintenance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (PRP) is the registry in which the resident agent and registered office are recorded; no annual form is fyled, but the registered agent must hold current annual confirmations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; annual agent confirmation and updated registry documents must be available whenever the Public Registry or DGI requires
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of a registered agent leads to inability to transact before the Public Registry and renders the corporation subject to administrative dissolution in Panama.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a Panamanian licensed Public Accountant (Contador Público Autorizado) is required when the S.A. realizes gross Panama-source income exceeding US$500,000 in the preceding fiscal year, or when the DGI designates the S.A. as a large taxpayer and expressly demands audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as issued by the IASB and adopted in Panama for reporting entities; qualifying smaller entities may present financial statements under IFRS for SMEs, and the financial statements must be accompanied by a Panamanian CPA opinion when audit or tax filing requirements apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 23 of 2015, the resident agent must obtain, maintain, and periodically update the beneficial ownership information of the S.A. at the registered office. Shareholders must provide updated UBO information to the agent upon any share transfer and no less frequently than annually at the ordinary meeting. Panama does not maintain a public beneficial ownership register.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$350 to US$700 per year for resident agent, registered office, and basic corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,000 to US$6,000 per year for a straightforward EMR SaaS corporation with moderate transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial corporate income tax (ISLR) system. No statutory tax holiday or software-sector preferential deduction applies to an EMR/SaaS Sociedad Anónima; Panama-source subscription revenue is taxable at the 25% headline rate. Foreign-source clause: licence fees and cloud hosting revenue from non-Panamanian medical clients are generally excluded from taxable income if the economic activity producing them is performed abroad. Deductible operating losses, capital allowances and compliant transfer-pricing allocations reduce the effective Panama tax base; a zero-liability return remains mandatory in loss years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 345 (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI e-Tax 2.0 portal (Dirección General de Ingresos, Panama).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance estimated ISLR payments and monthly withholding return for payroll/services.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year EMR company, the return and full settlement are due on or before March 31.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from Panamanian-source EMR clinical workflow subscriptions, implementation services, and medical-document digitisation fees received via Stripe Billing and bank transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income sourced in Panama. A non-resident-owned S.A. should exclude foreign SaaS use/licensing fees invoiced from a foreign affinity company, supported by transfer-pricing delineation; if no Panama-source sales exist, enter zero and file a nil declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claimed deductions directly attributable to Panama-source revenue: cloud hosting, personnel, medical-data compliance, legal/tax fees and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses paid by the Panamanian entity. Intra-group service or IP recharge must satisfy the arm's-length standard; unsupported offshore head-office allocations are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Panama-source net income after cost-of-sales and deductible expenses, then reduced by prior-year tax losses within the 5-year carryforward window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply DGI transfer-pricing adjustments if related-party considerations deviate from the CUP/TNMM benchmark; losses of a predecessor off-shore entity are not automatically portable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Headline corporate tax: 25% of Box 3 taxable net income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No preferential corporate rate exists for non-resident shareholders; the full 25% is payable even if profits are permanently retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance ISLR instalments and taxes withheld by Panamanian customers on clinical/EMR service invoices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support credits with Form 366 certificates issued by the withholding agent; over-payments create a refundable balance, whereas under-payment triggers interest.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Impuesto por Pagar / Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable after advance and withholding credits; zero and negative balances must still be reconciled in the e-Tax return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Finalise payment via automated bank debit or Panama National Bank payment voucher; late settlement of a nil return is subject to a fixed B/.100.00 penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine of 10% of the tax due, minimum B/.100.00, plus monthly interest of 1% (12% annual) on unpaid tax and a further statutory recargo (surcharge) of up to 50% for omissions. Fraudulent or false returns attract a 100% surcharge and criminal tax-fraud proceedings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends paid by a Panama S.A. out of Panama-source profits. Since risk profits carry an effective pre-dividend cost of 25%, the combined corporate-plus-dividend burden on a fully distributed Panama-source profit equals 32.5% of pre-tax profit (25% CIT + 10% WHT on after-tax dividend).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Reduced treaty rates are not automatic. The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the treaty counterpart tax administration in the 12 months preceding the payment and file the DGI's relief application (Solicitud de Exoneración de Retención/DTA claim) with the paying Panamanian S.A. The payer retains the statutory rate unless DGI confirms the reduced treaty rate; after confirmation, a refund of any excess withheld is obtained using the procedure for reimbursement of erroneous withholdings. If the EMR S.A. is a hybrid treated differently by the DTA partner, LOB (Limitation on Benefits) substantiation is mandatory.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory Panama-source withholding on gross payments for use of/right to use software, patents and know-how used in Panama; Panama's modern DTAs commonly reduce software royalties to 5% (often 0% for fully alienated software). Debt interest: 5% statutory withholding on Panama-source interest paid to non-resident related lenders; treaty rates typically 5% (bank-interest exemptions apply in several DTAs).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Balboa (PAB) / USD par: Local File must be prepared when related-party transactions exceed B/.5,000,000 in the tax period; Master File applies when group consolidated revenue exceeds B/.50,000,000; CbC reporting applies to significant groups with consolidated revenue above B/.850,000,000. The annual TP Informative Return (Form 380) is additionally triggered when Panama-source gross revenues exceed B/.12,000,000. For the current EMR SaaS business, the realistically critical threshold is B/.5,000,000 of intra-group clinical licensing/hosting flows.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama imposes Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) under Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 582 of 2021 only on 'relevant activities' (banking, insurance, IP holding, distribution, shipping, logistics, HQ, etc.). An active EMR clinical software vendor is outside the ESR perimeter. However, for territorial tax certainty and against the 'zero-tax shell S.A.' archetype, the company must demonstrate continuous Panamanian management, board meetings, medical-support staff, cloud procurement decisions, and an actual registered office. If the S.A. owns the EMR IP, all critical IP decision-making and exploitation functions must be in Panama; otherwise a foreign taxing authority or DGI can recharacterise the entity as a sham, re-source the SaaS income, and deny treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Redirecting Panama medical-clinic subscription fees to foreign bank accounts controlled by the beneficial owner while filing a nil or understated Form 345; fabricating cloud-hosting expenses; issuing false reseller invoices to strip taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 100% of the omitted corporate income tax plus 1% monthly interest; criminal tax-fraud charges punishable by imprisonment from 2 to 5 years and fines from two to ten times the tax covered.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign fraudulent returns are jointly and severally liable for unpaid taxes, interest and penalties; courts may issue additional travel bans (prohibición de salida) and attach personal assets for civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated royalties, 'software maintenance' fees, or clinical consulting charges to a related BVI/Cayman/Panama foundation without economic substance; failing to file Form 380 or prepare Local/Master Files when thresholds are exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjusts taxable income to arm's length, imposes a 100% surcharge on the tax undercharged for abusive related-party transactions, and levies documentation fines of B/.1,000-B/.5,000 per omitted TP report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers/tax directors who sign non-arm's-length contracts are personally responsible for the DGI adjustment if the company is insolvent; in fraud cases, personal criminal liability and travel restrictions follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Panama S.A. only as an 'invoice pass-through' for offshore medical software developers: no office, no Panamanian operational decision-making, no employees, and no bank account in Panama, with all revenue function exercised outside Panama.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI and courts may disregard the entity for tax purposes, re-source all EMR SaaS income to a taxable permanent establishment, impose the 25% ISLR plus recargo of 50%, suspend the corporate licence, and order dissolution of the S.A.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under the doctrine of 'levantamiento del velo societario', directors and shadow owners are personally liable for corporate tax debt; criminal sanctions for fraud and court-imposed travel bans may accompany the civil recovery.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file or annually update the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration in the Panama registry; processing large monthly Stripe volumes without maintaining source-of-funds files; transacting with shell suppliers or nominees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines of up to B/.500,000 under Law 129 of 2020 and Law 23 of 2015 for UBO/AML omissions; the S.A. may be included in the public beneficial-ownership non-compliant list, incurring commercial-banking restrictions and director disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: De facto directors and compliance officers can be criminally prosecuted for money-laundering facilitation (5 to 12 years imprisonment), personal fines, seizure of foreign assets, and travel bans while under investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Remitting US$45,000 annual EMR SaaS profits to beneficial shareholders without applying the 10% dividend withholding tax; using 'foreign-source profit' declarations to avoid WHT without corroborating territorial-source analysis; paying dividends while the S.A. is technically insolvent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withholding agent is liable for the 10% unpaid WHT plus a recargo of 10% to 25%, interest at 1% monthly, and, if the distribution was made in resort of fraud, criminal fines; the dividend payment may be clawed back for creditor protection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors authorising unlawful dividends are jointly and severally liable to the tax authority for the WHT and to creditors for the distributed value; serious or repeated violations expose them to criminal securities/fraud liability and travel bans.
